Noosa Triathlon Swim Leg Cancelled After Shark Sightings; Event Runs as Duathlon

02 Nov 2026, 06:34 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.abc.net.au

3 min read

Key takeaways

  2. Shark Sightings Prompt Cancellation

Event Overview

  • The 2026 Noosa Triathlon, recognised as the world’s largest Olympic‑distance triathlon, was scheduled to host 8,500 athletes and attract roughly 20,000 spectators.
  • The sold‑out event was set to begin at 6:15 am on Sunday at Noosa Main Beach, Queensland.

Shark Sightings Prompt Cancellation

  • Surf lifesavers monitoring the course reported a shark sighting at first light on Sunday, approximately one hour before the planned start.
  • Lifesavers, who were to patrol on jet skis and boards, declined to enter the water following the sighting.
  • Organisers had already reduced the swim distance to about 1 km on Saturday night after earlier sightings, but the Sunday morning sighting forced a complete cancellation of the swim leg.

Safety Protocols and Decision Timeline

  • Surf Lifesaving Queensland’s protocol requires a 60‑minute clearance after the last shark sighting before anyone enters the water.
  • With the sighting occurring an hour before the race start, there was insufficient time to delay the event further.
  • Head of operations Rebecca Van Pooss confirmed the decision was unprecedented in the event’s 43‑year history, though contingency adjustments to course design have occurred previously.

Race Converted to Duathlon

  • The competition proceeded as a duathlon: a 5 km run replaced the 1.5 km swim, followed by the standard 40 km cycle and 10 km run.
  • Athletes had minimal time to recalibrate race plans after the late‑morning announcement.

Elite Results

  • Men’s elite: Matt Hauser defended his 2025 title, finishing in 1:39:34.
  • Women’s elite: Natalie Van Coevorden won in 1:58:11, edging out Richelle Hill by 15 seconds.

Official Statements

  • Rebecca Van Pooss (Noosa Triathlon head of operations): “We knew that it was a potential this morning, so we had a contingency plan ready to go… based on that decision, we made our decision that we also can’t put athletes in the water.”
  • Matt Thompson (Surf Lifesaving Queensland safety manager): “The best outcome is always preventing an incident before it happens, and the ability to identify potential threats early and act quickly is critical to keeping Queenslanders safe in the water.”

Practical Implications for Participants

  • Athletes should review race‑day communications for last‑minute course changes, especially in coastal events where marine life activity can alter safety plans.
  • Event organisers may adopt similar contingency frameworks (alternative run segments, shortened swims) for future editions.
  • Spectators and support crews need to stay informed via official channels for real‑time updates on course modifications.

How to Verify the Announcement

  • Consult the original ABC News report (published 1 November 2026) for the primary account.
  • Check the official Noosa Triathlon website and social media for organiser statements.
  • Review Surf Lifesaving Queensland’s public safety advisories regarding shark‑related beach closures.
